- When sentiment is high (≥0.7), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to compensate.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes; apply a 1–3 day lag correction after sharp upward moves.  
- After a 3–5 day downtrend, model frequently undercorrects; add 1–2% upward bias to avoid mean reversion trap.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overshoots early in the horizon; cap forecast at 10–15% above 14-day moving average.  
- If sentiment history shows rapid swings, reduce forecast volatility by 20–40% to avoid overfitting to noise.
